nodes.name: Order of $a$ modulo $r$
nodes.statement: Given $r \in \mathbb{N}$, $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $(a,r)=1$, the order of $a$ modulo $r$, denoted $o_r(a)$, is the smallest $k$ such that $a^k = 1 \pmod{r}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The order of a modulo r is the smallest positive k with a^k congruent to 1 mod r.

nodes.name: Euler's totient function $\phi(r)$
nodes.statement: For $r \in \mathbb{N}$, $\phi(r)$ is the number of integers less than $r$ that are relatively prime to $r$. For any $a$ with $(a,r)=1$, $o_r(a) \mid \phi(r)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Euler's totient counts integers below r coprime to r.

nodes.name: Soft-O notation $O^{\sim}$
nodes.statement: $O^{\sim}(t(n)) = O(t(n) \cdot \mathrm{poly}(\log t(n)))$. For instance $O^{\sim}(\log^k n) = O(\log^k n \cdot \mathrm{poly}(\log\log n))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Soft-O hides polylogarithmic factors in the running-time bound.

nodes.name: Introspective number for a polynomial
nodes.statement: For a polynomial $f(X)$ and number $m \in \mathbb{N}$, $m$ is introspective for $f(X)$ if $[f(X)]^m = f(X^m) \pmod{X^r - 1, p}$.
nodes.statement_clean: m is introspective for f if raising f to the m-th power equals composing f with X^m, modulo X^r-1 and p.

nodes.name: Sophie-Germain primes
nodes.statement: A prime $q$ is a Sophie-Germain prime if $2q+1$ is also prime.
nodes.statement_clean: A prime q is Sophie-Germain when 2q+1 is also prime.

nodes.name: Set $I$ of introspective numbers
nodes.statement: $I = \{(\tfrac{n}{p})^i \cdot p^j \mid i, j \geq 0\}$. Every member of $I$ is introspective for every polynomial in $P$.
nodes.statement_clean: I is the multiplicative set generated by n/p and p; its members are introspective for all polynomials in P.

nodes.name: Set $P$ of polynomials
nodes.statement: $P = \{ \prod_{a=0}^{\ell} (X+a)^{e_a} \mid e_a \geq 0 \}$ where $\ell = \lfloor \sqrt{\phi(r)} \log n \rfloor$.
nodes.statement_clean: P is the multiplicative monoid generated by the linear factors X, X+1, ..., X+l.

nodes.name: Group $G$ (residues of $I$ mod $r$)
nodes.statement: $G$ is the subgroup of $\mathbb{Z}_r^*$ formed by residues modulo $r$ of numbers in $I$. Generated by $n$ and $p$ mod $r$; size $t = |G| > \log^2 n$ since $o_r(n) > \log^2 n$.
nodes.statement_clean: G is the subgroup of (Z/rZ)* generated by n and p modulo r.

nodes.name: Group $\mathcal{G}$ (residues of $P$ in $F$)
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{G}$ is the multiplicative subgroup of $F = \mathbb{F}_p[X]/(h(X))$ generated by $X, X+1, \ldots, X+\ell$, where $h(X)$ is an irreducible factor of the cyclotomic polynomial $Q_r(X)$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$.
nodes.statement_clean: G-script is the multiplicative subgroup of the field F generated by the linear elements X+a, 0 <= a <= l.

nodes.name: Polynomial identity for primes (Lemma 2.1)
nodes.statement: Let $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $n \geq 2$, $(a,n)=1$. Then $n$ is prime iff $(X+a)^n = X^n + a \pmod{n}$.
nodes.statement_clean: n is prime iff the polynomial congruence (X+a)^n equals X^n+a modulo n.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Examine binomial coefficients in $((X+a)^n - (X^n+a))$: the coefficient of $X^i$ for $0<i<n$ is $\binom{n}{i} a^{n-i}$. If $n$ is prime, $\binom{n}{i} \equiv 0 \pmod n$. If $n$ is composite, pick a prime $q$ with $q^k \| n$; then $q^k \nmid \binom{n}{q}$, so the coefficient of $X^q$ is nonzero mod $n$.

nodes.name: LCM lower bound (Lemma 3.1)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{LCM}(m)$ denote the lcm of the first $m$ numbers. For $m \geq 7$, $\mathrm{LCM}(m) \geq 2^m$.
nodes.statement_clean: The lcm of 1,2,...,m grows at least as 2^m for m >= 7.

nodes.name: Correctness of AKS algorithm (Theorem 4.1)
nodes.statement: The algorithm returns PRIME if and only if $n$ is prime.
nodes.statement_clean: The AKS algorithm correctly classifies n as PRIME exactly when n is prime.
conclusions: AKS outputs PRIME $\iff n$ is prime

nodes.name: AKS Algorithm for Primality Testing
nodes.statement: Deterministic polynomial-time primality test based on a polynomial identity in $\mathbb{Z}_n[X]/(X^r-1)$.
nodes.statement_clean: AKS deterministic polynomial-time primality test.
nodes.pseudocode: 1. If $n = a^b$ for $a \in \mathbb{N}$ and $b > 1$, output COMPOSITE. 2. Find the smallest $r$ such that $o_r(n) > \log^2 n$. 3. If $1 < (a,n) < n$ for some $a \leq r$, output COMPOSITE. 4. If $n \leq r$, output PRIME. 5. For $a = 1$ to $\lfloor \sqrt{\phi(r)} \log n \rfloor$ do: if $(X+a)^n \neq X^n + a \pmod{X^r-1, n}$, output COMPOSITE. 6. Output PRIME.

nodes.name: Perfect-power test
nodes.statement: If $n = a^b$ for some $a \in \mathbb{N}$ and $b > 1$, output COMPOSITE.

nodes.name: Find suitable $r$
nodes.statement: Find the smallest $r$ such that $o_r(n) > \log^2 n$.

nodes.name: Small-factor sieve up to $r$
nodes.statement: If $1 < (a,n) < n$ for some $a \leq r$, output COMPOSITE.

nodes.name: Small-$n$ shortcut
nodes.statement: If $n \leq r$, output PRIME.

nodes.name: Polynomial-identity loop
nodes.statement: For $a = 1$ to $\lfloor \sqrt{\phi(r)} \log n \rfloor$: if $(X+a)^n \neq X^n + a \pmod{X^r - 1, n}$, output COMPOSITE.

nodes.name: Output PRIME
nodes.statement: Output PRIME.

nodes.name: Soundness on primes (Lemma 4.2)
nodes.statement: If $n$ is prime, the algorithm returns PRIME.
nodes.statement_clean: If n is prime then AKS outputs PRIME.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement: If $n$ is prime, steps 1 and 3 cannot return COMPOSITE. By Lemma 2.1, the for-loop also cannot return COMPOSITE. Hence the algorithm outputs PRIME at step 4 or step 6.

nodes.name: Existence of small $r$ (Lemma 4.3)
nodes.statement: There exists $r \leq \max\{3, \lceil \log^5 n \rceil\}$ such that $o_r(n) > \log^2 n$.
nodes.statement_clean: A suitable r of size O(log^5 n) always exists.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement: For $n=2$, $r=3$ works. For $n>2$, set $B=\lceil \log^5 n \rceil > 10$ so Lemma 3.1 applies. Show that $n^{\lfloor \log B \rfloor} \cdot \prod_{i=1}^{\lfloor \log^2 n \rfloor} (n^i-1) < 2^B \leq \mathrm{LCM}(B)$, so the smallest $r$ not dividing this product satisfies $r \leq B$, $(r,n)=1$, and $o_r(n) > \log^2 n$.

nodes.name: Closure under multiplication (Lemma 4.5)
nodes.statement: If $m$ and $m'$ are introspective for $f(X)$, then so is $m \cdot m'$.
nodes.statement_clean: Introspective numbers for f form a multiplicative set.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.5
nodes.statement: From $[f(X)]^{m m'} = [f(X^m)]^{m'} \pmod{X^r - 1, p}$ and substituting $X \mapsto X^m$ in the introspection equation for $m'$ we get $[f(X^m)]^{m'} = f(X^{m m'}) \pmod{X^{m r} - 1, p}$, which yields $f(X^{m m'}) \pmod{X^r - 1, p}$ since $X^r - 1 \mid X^{m r} - 1$.

nodes.name: Closure under product of polynomials (Lemma 4.6)
nodes.statement: If $m$ is introspective for $f(X)$ and $g(X)$, then $m$ is introspective for $f(X) \cdot g(X)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Polynomials for which m is introspective form a multiplicative set.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.6
nodes.statement: $[f(X) g(X)]^m = [f(X)]^m \cdot [g(X)]^m = f(X^m) \cdot g(X^m) \pmod{X^r - 1, p}$.

nodes.name: Lower bound on $|\mathcal{G}|$ (Lemma 4.7, Lenstra)
nodes.statement: $|\mathcal{G}| \geq \binom{t+\ell}{t-1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: G-script has at least binomial(t+l, t-1) elements.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.7
nodes.statement: Show two distinct polynomials of degree $<t$ in $P$ give distinct elements of $\mathcal{G}$: if $f(X)=g(X)$ in $F$, then $f(X^m)=g(X^m)$ for all $m \in G$, giving $t$ distinct roots of $Q(Y)=f(Y)-g(Y)$ in $F$, contradicting $\deg Q < t$. Counting linear factors $X+a$, there are $\ell+1$ distinct degree-1 polynomials in $\mathcal{G}$, hence $\binom{t+\ell}{t-1}$ distinct polynomials of degree $<t$.

nodes.name: Distinct polynomials map to distinct elements
nodes.statement: Two distinct polynomials of degree $<t$ in $P$ yield distinct elements of $\mathcal{G}$, by considering $Q(Y)=f(Y)-g(Y)$ which has $t$ roots $X^m$ in $F$ when $f=g$ in $F$ — a contradiction since $\deg Q < t$.

nodes.name: Distinct linear factors $X+a$
nodes.statement: Since $\ell < r$ and $p > r$, the elements $X, X+1, \ldots, X+\ell$ are pairwise distinct and nonzero in $F$, giving $\ell+1$ distinct linear elements of $\mathcal{G}$.

nodes.name: Counting argument: $\binom{t+\ell}{t-1}$ polynomials
nodes.statement: Count distinct polynomials of degree $<t$ in $\ell+1$ variables-as-factors: at least $\binom{t+\ell}{t-1}$ such polynomials, each giving a distinct element of $\mathcal{G}$.

nodes.name: Upper bound on $|\mathcal{G}|$ (Lemma 4.8, Kalai-Sahai-Sudan)
nodes.statement: If $n$ is not a power of $p$, then $|\mathcal{G}| \leq n^{\sqrt{t}}$.
nodes.statement_clean: When n is not a prime power, G-script has at most n^sqrt(t) elements.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.8
nodes.statement: Consider $\hat{I} = \{(n/p)^i p^j \mid 0 \leq i,j \leq \lfloor\sqrt{t}\rfloor\}$. If $n$ is not a power of $p$, $|\hat{I}| > t = |G|$, so two elements $m_1 > m_2$ collide modulo $r$. Then every $f(X) \in \mathcal{G}$ is a root of $Q'(Y) = Y^{m_1} - Y^{m_2}$ in $F$. Since $\deg Q' = m_1 \leq n^{\sqrt{t}}$, we get $|\mathcal{G}| \leq n^{\sqrt{t}}$.

nodes.name: Construct $\hat{I}$ and force a collision
nodes.statement: Define $\hat{I} = \{(n/p)^i p^j \mid 0 \leq i,j \leq \lfloor\sqrt{t}\rfloor\}$; if $n$ is not a power of $p$, $|\hat{I}| > t$ forces two elements $m_1 > m_2$ with $X^{m_1} = X^{m_2} \pmod{X^r-1}$.

nodes.name: Every element of $\mathcal{G}$ is a root of $Q'$
nodes.statement: Use introspection: $[f(X)]^{m_1} = [f(X)]^{m_2}$ in $F$ for every $f \in P$, so $f(X)$ is a root of $Q'(Y) = Y^{m_1}-Y^{m_2}$.

nodes.name: Bound $|\mathcal{G}|$ by $\deg Q'$
nodes.statement: $|\mathcal{G}| \leq \deg Q' = m_1 \leq n^{\sqrt{t}}$.

nodes.name: Soundness on composites (Lemma 4.9)
nodes.statement: If the algorithm returns PRIME then $n$ is prime.
nodes.statement_clean: If AKS outputs PRIME, n is prime.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.9 (squeeze argument)
nodes.statement: Combine Lemma 4.7 lower bound $|\mathcal{G}| \geq \binom{t+\ell}{t-1} > n^{\sqrt{t}}$ with Lemma 4.8 upper bound $|\mathcal{G}| \leq n^{\sqrt{t}}$ when $n$ is not a power of $p$. The contradiction forces $n = p^k$; step 1 rules out $k > 1$, so $n = p$.

nodes.name: Lower bound on $|\mathcal{G}|$
nodes.statement: By Lemma 4.7 and arithmetic on $\binom{t+\ell}{t-1}$ using $t > \sqrt{t}\log n$ and $\ell = \lfloor \sqrt{\phi(r)}\log n\rfloor \geq \lfloor \sqrt{t}\log n\rfloor$: $|\mathcal{G}| > 2^{\lfloor \sqrt{t}\log n\rfloor + 1} \geq n^{\sqrt{t}}$.

nodes.name: Contradiction with upper bound
nodes.statement: By Lemma 4.8, $|\mathcal{G}| \leq n^{\sqrt{t}}$ when $n$ is not a power of $p$, contradicting the lower bound. Hence $n = p^k$.

nodes.name: Step 1 rules out $k > 1$
nodes.statement: If $k > 1$, the perfect-power test in step 1 outputs COMPOSITE, contradicting the assumption that AKS returned PRIME. Hence $k=1$ and $n=p$.

nodes.name: Time complexity $O^{\sim}(\log^{21/2} n)$ (Theorem 5.1)
nodes.statement: The asymptotic time complexity of the AKS algorithm is $O^{\sim}(\log^{21/2} n)$.
nodes.statement_clean: AKS runs in soft-O of log^(21/2) n bit operations.
assumptions: Use FFT-based arithmetic for integer/polynomial multiplication

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.1
nodes.statement: Step 1: $O^{\sim}(\log^3 n)$. Step 2: $O^{\sim}(\log^7 n)$ (try $O(\log^5 n)$ values of $r$, each requiring $O(\log^2 n)$ multiplications mod $r$). Step 3: $O(\log^6 n)$ gcds. Step 5 dominates: $O^{\sim}(r^2 \log^2 n)$ per equation times $\sqrt{\phi(r)}\log n$ equations gives $O^{\sim}(r^{3/2} \log^3 n) = O^{\sim}(\log^{21/2} n)$.

nodes.name: Fouvry's density bound (Lemma 5.2)
nodes.statement: There exist constants $c > 0$ and $n_0$ such that, for all $x \geq n_0$: $|\{q \mid q \text{ prime}, q \leq x, P(q-1) > q^{2/3}\}| \geq c \cdot \frac{x}{\ln x}$.
nodes.statement_clean: A positive density of primes q have a large prime factor of q-1 exceeding q^(2/3).
conclusions: At least $c \cdot x/\ln x$ primes $q \leq x$ satisfy $P(q-1) > q^{2/3}$

nodes.name: Improved time complexity $O^{\sim}(\log^{15/2} n)$ (Theorem 5.3)
nodes.statement: The asymptotic time complexity of the AKS algorithm is $O^{\sim}(\log^{15/2} n)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Using Fouvry's density bound, the running time improves to soft-O of log^(15/2) n.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.3
nodes.statement: By Lemma 5.2, the high density of primes $q$ with $P(q-1) > q^{2/3}$ guarantees that step 2 finds $r = O(\log^3 n)$ with $o_r(n) > \log^2 n$. Substituting into the bound from Theorem 5.1 yields $O^{\sim}(\log^{15/2} n)$.

nodes.name: Artin's Conjecture
nodes.statement: Given $n \in \mathbb{N}$ not a perfect square, the number of primes $q \leq m$ with $o_q(n) = q-1$ is asymptotically $A(n) \cdot m/\ln m$, where $A(n) > 0.35$ is Artin's constant.
nodes.statement_clean: Asymptotic density of primes for which n is a primitive root is positive.

nodes.name: Sophie-Germain Prime Density Conjecture
nodes.statement: The number of primes $q \leq m$ such that $2q+1$ is also prime is asymptotically $2C_2 \cdot m / \ln^2 m$, where $C_2 \approx 0.66$ is the twin-prime constant.
nodes.statement_clean: Sophie-Germain primes have positive asymptotic density given by the twin-prime constant.

nodes.name: Agrawal's Conjecture (BP01/KS02)
nodes.statement: If $r$ is a prime not dividing $n$ and $(X-1)^n = X^n - 1 \pmod{X^r - 1, n}$, then either $n$ is prime or $n^2 = 1 \pmod{r}$.
nodes.statement_clean: A single polynomial identity at one a=-1 should suffice to detect primality (modulo a small exceptional condition).
nodes.notes: Lenstra-Pomerance gave heuristic argument suggesting this is false; variants may still hold.

nodes.name: Heuristic complexity $O^{\sim}(\log^6 n)$ under Sophie-Germain density
nodes.statement: Under the Sophie-Germain prime density conjecture, $r = O^{\sim}(\log^2 n)$ and the algorithm runs in $O^{\sim}(\log^6 n)$ time.
nodes.statement_clean: If Sophie-Germain conjecture holds, AKS runs in soft-O of log^6 n.

nodes.name: Lenstra-Pomerance unconditional $O^{\sim}(\log^6 n)$
nodes.statement: Lenstra and Pomerance [LP03a] gave a modified version of the algorithm with provable time complexity $O^{\sim}(\log^6 n)$.
nodes.statement_clean: A modified AKS variant achieves provable soft-O of log^6 n.

nodes.name: Conditional $O^{\sim}(\log^3 n)$ under Agrawal's conjecture
nodes.statement: If Agrawal's conjecture holds, one can search for $r \in [2, 4\log n]$ not dividing $n^2-1$ and verify a single congruence in $O^{\sim}(r \log^2 n) = O^{\sim}(\log^3 n)$ time.
nodes.statement_clean: Agrawal's conjecture would enable an even faster O~(log^3 n) algorithm.

nodes.name: Polynomial identity (1)
nodes.statement: $(X+a)^n = X^n + a \pmod{n}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The base polynomial identity for primality.

nodes.name: Modular polynomial identity (2)
nodes.statement: $(X+a)^n = X^n + a \pmod{X^r - 1, n}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Polynomial identity reduced modulo X^r-1, the form actually tested by the algorithm.

nodes.name: PRIMES decision problem
nodes.statement: Decide whether a given input integer $n$ is prime or composite. Goal: deterministic polynomial-time algorithm in the input size $\lceil \log n \rceil$.
nodes.statement_clean: Decide primality of n in time polynomial in log n.

nodes.name: Fermat's Little Theorem
nodes.statement: For any prime $p$ and any $a$ with $p \nmid a$, $a^{p-1} = 1 \pmod{p}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Fermat's Little Theorem on prime power residues.

nodes.name: Cyclotomic factorization over $\mathbb{F}_p$
nodes.statement: $Q_r(X)$, the $r$-th cyclotomic polynomial over $\mathbb{F}_p$, divides $X^r - 1$ and factors into irreducible factors each of degree $o_r(p)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Cyclotomic polynomials over F_p factor into degree o_r(p) irreducibles.
